subject: Proposal: move from monthly billing to annual prepay — pricing, ramp and concessions
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah@avasolutions.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement <procurement@avasolutions.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Re-evaluating billing cadence — interest in annual prepay

Ben,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We ran a quick internal ROI review and are strongly leaning toward consolidating our usage onto an annual prepay model rather than continuing with monthly invoices. Two quick asks as we scope this: 1) what level of term discount can you offer for a 12-month prepay at our current run-rate (~$50k/month today), and 2) can you outline a ramp schedule / credit usage approach if we commit to a stepped increase over the first 18 months?

Our procurement team also wants visibility into any one-time concessions (onboarding credits, trial overages) you might include to smooth the move. If you can get a high-level worksheet together today/tomorrow that would be great — Tom (cc) will need something he can take to finance.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lim
Head of Platform Operations | Ava Solutions

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah@avasolutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating billing cadence — interest in annual prepay

Sarah — appreciate the clarity. Short answers up front: we can do an annual prepay with a tiered term discount (higher committed spend / multi-year gets to a deeper discount) and we can propose a ramp schedule that lets you prepay at a conservative level and apply true-ups as usage grows.

I attached a pricing worksheet (redwood_ava_pricing_v3.xlsx) with two models:
- Conservative ramp: Year 1 prepay = $500k (approx. 10x current monthly) with an 15% term discount; true-up at mid-year if usage exceeds prepay.
- Growth ramp: Year 1 prepay = $600k with staged commitments to $1.2M by Year 3; starts at 18% discount year 1 and steps to 22% for the multi-year aggregate.

We can also include one-time onboarding credits equal to 5% of year-1 prepay if you sign within 14 days. That credit can be applied to overage or professional services.

Two asks from our side: 1) can finance confirm Ava can accept an annual prepay SC/PO and 2) legal will need a standard SOW + any procurement redlines (we can handle via DocuSign). If this looks promising I’ll loop Dylan (rev ops) to build an executed CODA and Marissa (AM) to propose an implementation schedule.

Next steps: I’m available for a quick call Monday to walk through the worksheet and lock a target prepay.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 11:45 AM PST
Subject: Fwd: Re-evaluating billing cadence — interest in annual prepay

Ben — quick internal note. Finance is OK with annual prepay but requires: (a) a clean PO with billing contact and tax details, (b) wire instructions and bank verification before first invoice, and (c) an approval for onboarding credit > $25k to come from me/AM budget sign-off.

Dylan — can you prepare a payment schedule for the two models Ben attached and include our preferred ACH and wire terms? Monica, please flag any CS risks for a big year-1 true-up.

Marissa
Senior Account Director | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Elliott <tom.elliott@avasolutions.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Sarah Lim <sarah@avasolutions.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 08:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating billing cadence — interest in annual prepay

Ben, Sarah — I reviewed the worksheet. A couple of finance constraints to call out from our side: Ava prefers to avoid big up-front cash commits without staged deliverables. We would consider: a 12-month prepay at 50% upfront and 50% at month 6, OR a quarterly drawdown from a committed annual bucket (both options still billed/recognized as prepaid for accounting). We’ll need to see refund / credit terms if usage undershoots by >20% year-over-year.

Also — we do expect a concession on net price for an annual move; 15% minimum, 20% preferred. The onboarding credit will help but won’t replace the list discount target.

If you can model 50% upfront option plus 20% discount at the $600k Y1 prepay and show how true-ups/refunds would work, we can expedite review.

Tom
CFO | Ava Solutions

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Tom Elliott <tom.elliott@avasolutions.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah@avasolutions.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.example>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 10:05 AM PST
Subject: Re: Re-evaluating billing cadence — interest in annual prepay

Tom — thanks, that is helpful. We can absolutely structure a 50/50 split (50% due on signature, 50% billed at month 6) and model a pro-rata refund/credit if annual usage is <80% of committed bucket (refunds net of transaction costs; credits for months 7–12 otherwise).

Based on internal approvals, here is our revised commercial proposal (summary):
- Year 1 prepay: $600,000 (50% upfront / 50% at month 6)
- Year 1 effective discount: 20% off standard pay-as-you-go list for committed units
- Ramp: optional Year 2 commitment to $900k, Year 3 to $1.2M with step-up discounts (22% year-2+, add'l marketing credit if multi-year signed)
- Onboarding credit: 5% of year-1 prepay ($30k) applied to professional services or overage credits if signed within 10 business days
- Refund/true-up: if actual usage < 80% of prepay, refund/credit for unused portion pro-rated; if usage > prepay, overage billed at discounted rate

I attached a redlined Mutual Action Plan and an SOW draft (mutual_action_plan_Ava-RW.pdf, Ava-SOW-draft.docx). If this looks acceptable I can route a DocuSign package (pricing + SOW) and we can set an internal target to execute by Jan 22 to hit our onboarding window.

Would you like a 20-minute call today to walk finance through the refund mechanics?

Thanks,
Ben

From: Sarah Lim <sarah@avasolutions.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Elliott <tom.elliott@avasolutions.com>, procurement <procurement@avasolutions.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 5:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Proposal: move from monthly billing to annual prepay — pricing, ramp and concessions

Ben — all good progress here. Tom and I reviewed the revised commercial proposal with procurement. High-level feedback: 1) Tom approves the 50/50 billing cadence and 20% discount at $600k Y1 as long as refund/credit mechanics are explicit in the SOW, 2) procurement wants the onboarding credit to be applied as a pre-billed credit on invoice 1 rather than as PS credit, and 3) Ava legal has two small redlines on termination language — sending separately.

Please send the DocuSign package with the updated invoice-credit language and we’ll aim to turn around signatures within 72 hours. Appreciate the fast cadence.

Sarah
